title: Fasten a bracket bolt with a ratchet in confined access
instruction: Use the fitted socket ratchet to tighten the started bracket bolt with short back-and-forth strokes between the walls until the bolt is seated.
context: Confined maintenance work requires repeated short drive and return strokes when surrounding structure prevents a full wrench turn.
setup: Dual YAM station. The right gripper initially holds a 203 mm ratchet with a fitted 13.4 mm AF steel socket on an M8x16 steel bolt (1.25 mm pitch, 14 g). The bolt is threaded into a fixed steel receiver under a 3 mm steel bracket with a 2.5 mm under-head gap. Two 162 mm high, 9 mm thick steel walls restrict swing to about ±16 degrees. The left arm starts clear. Flat rubber grip pads provide contact purchase. Exact SI poses and geometry are in ratchet_task/config.py and build_assets.py.
scoring: Current-state score: 0.2 after 0.25 clockwise turns; 0.4 after 1 turn; 0.7 after at least 1.8 turns and an under-head gap within -0.3/+0.2 mm. Full credit requires that seated state with socket engagement for 0.5 s and at least 6 drive/return cycles with actual bolt advance. Initial setup earns zero. Integrity faults and >1 N m contact torque invalidate the trial.
reset_notes: Reset restores the threaded bolt, fitted socket and initial contact grasp. All placement jigs are removed before policy actions.
fidelity: NVIDIA ratchet visuals plus original metric socket, bolt and fixture. Physical hex contacts transmit torque; a native one-way clutch and pitch joint drive rotation and axial travel. Thread ridges are visual; tooth impacts, deformation and fastener strength are omitted. The robot starts holding the fitted ratchet on a threaded bolt. Reset placement jigs are removed before actions. Tightening is judged by seating and ratchet cycles.
